description: Use after search_archive, whats_new, what_changed, get_topic_brief or contextualize_url to read one record in full: metadata (dates, topics, source URLs, primary_source_url) and the body as Markdown (capped; see truncated). Pass any newruntime.com record URL they return (notes, signals, analyses, patterns, shifts, systems, projects, topics, tools, guides, sources), or kind + slug. level "short" returns only the title, dates, summary, topics, first source URLs, primary source and routes (2-3 KB instead of up to 60 KB; no body): use it to triage several records, then read the ones you keep at the default level "full". Free, no auth. Example: {"url": "https://newruntime.com/patterns/company-memory-needs-write-loops/", "level": "short"}.

level.description: full (default): metadata and the body as Markdown. short: title, dates, summary, topics, first sources and routes only.

name: get_record

body_chars.description: Length of the full body in characters.

body_markdown.description: Body text as Markdown, or null.

json_url.description: Machine-readable twin of the record, or null.

level.description: short when level short was asked; absent for the full record.

next.description: Level short: how to read the body.

primary_source_missing.description: True when every source of the record is secondary coverage.

primary_source_url.description: First source that is not press, newsletter or social coverage; null when the record cites none.

record.description: Metadata: title, dates, source_urls, topics, routes (level short: scalar fields, topics, first source URLs and routes only).

source_urls_total.description: Level short: how many source URLs the record cites when more than the five listed.

summary.description: Level short: one-paragraph summary, or null.

truncated.description: True when body_markdown was cut; markdown_url has it all.

title: Read one New Runtime record
